column1: # glob-overlap-vectors.tsv — executable form of the overlap contract
# TAB-separated, five columns. Blank lines and `#` lines are ignored.
#   2 surfaceA  the globs of surface A, separated by `;` (one per line in the
#               file handed to the script). `(none)` = an empty surface file.
#               An empty element (`a;;b`) becomes a blank line.
#   4 evidence  the EXACT expected stdout: pairs separated by `;`, each pair
#               written `<globA>><globB>` (the `>` stands for the TAB the script
#               emits). `-` on a `no` row = not applicable; stdout must be empty.
#               Evidence carries the NORMALIZED glob, not the raw input line.
#   5 desc      what this row pins down
# NO FIELD MAY BE EMPTY (adjacent tabs collapse during shell field splitting) —
# Exit-code-2 misuse, CRLF tolerance, and the entry-digest contract are not
# expressible here; run-tests.sh checks those directly.
# declared-surface-schema.md §1 truth table — all seven rows, verbatim

column5: §1 row 2 — B is under A subtree
§1 row 6 — * is one segment, B has an extra one

column1: # Normalization — omitted by the truth table, required by R6.5

column5: normalization does not manufacture an overlap
duplicate globs in one surface yield one evidence line

column1: # `?` — exactly one char, within one segment

column5: ? is one char, not a run
? unifies against * on the other side

column1: # `*` — a run of chars, within one segment

column5: * matches a run inside a segment
the literal tail must still unify

column1: # `**` — zero or more WHOLE segments (the zero-segment cases R6.5 names)
# Set-vs-set — the script unit is the SURFACE, every table row above is

column5: set-vs-set — exactly one of four pairs intersects
set-vs-set — two evidence lines, A-major order
an empty surface is disjoint from everything
